questionText: How do you configure HTTPS for the Spring Boot embedded server?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can configure a named SSL bundle for an embedded server, explain keystore and truststore roles, and choose between direct and proxy TLS termination.
inScope: One-way HTTPS versus mutual TLS trust
outOfScope: Committing private keys or literal passwords
A claim that a server truststore is required for ordinary one-way HTTPS

claims.statement: Spring Boot 3.3 can define named JKS or PEM SSL bundles and apply one to the embedded server using server.ssl.bundle.
The server keystore supplies its identity and private key; a server truststore is needed when the server verifies client certificates, such as mutual TLS.
TLS may terminate in the embedded server or at a trusted proxy, and forwarded information must only be trusted according to the deployment configuration.

examples.title: Mounted PKCS12 SSL bundle for the embedded server

validation.command: Focused embedded-server example gate parses SSL bundle and server keys and checks the environment placeholder
validation.expected: The named web bundle uses a mounted PKCS12 path, external password placeholder, and server.ssl.bundle reference

visuals.title: Direct embedded-server TLS versus trusted-proxy termination

notes: The content distinguishes server identity from client-certificate trust and never embeds a real secret.

review.notes: SSL bundle properties, key/trust roles, and embedded-server application were checked against official Spring Boot 3.3 SSL documentation. Deployment-specific proxy guidance is scoped as an operational boundary.
